Basic Hashing.theory: Hashing stores a count or an index per key. Use HashMap for unrestricted integer values; frequency arrays work only when the value range is small and explicitly bounded. Prefix sums plus a map count subarrays, including negatives. Expected O(1) operations rely on normal hashing assumptions.

Longest Consecutive Sequence in an Array.problem: Return the longest run of consecutive integer VALUES, regardless of input order. Duplicates do not extend a run.
Longest Consecutive Sequence in an Array.approach: Start expansion only where x-1 is absent. Each unique value is visited once by its run, so repeated expansions are avoided.
Longest Consecutive Sequence in an Array.trace: Start at 1 and walk 2,3,4: length 4. 100 and 200 each form length 1.
Longest Consecutive Sequence in an Array.pitfalls: Guard MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE before +/-1 to prevent wraparound.
Longest Consecutive Sequence in an Array.alternatives: Sort a copy and scan in O(n log n) time, ignoring duplicate values.

Longest subarray with sum K.problem: Return the maximum length of a contiguous subarray summing to k; empty/no match returns zero.
Longest subarray with sum K.approach: If prefix[i]-prefix[j]=k, subarray (j,i] sums to k. Keep the EARLIEST index of each prefix sum to maximize length. Seed prefix 0 at index -1.
Longest subarray with sum K.trace: Prefixes of [1,-1,2,-2,3] are 1,0,2,0,3; zero prefix at i=3 spans four values from index 0.
Longest subarray with sum K.pitfalls: Negative values invalidate ordinary sum-based sliding windows. Store prefix sums as long; overwriting earliest indices shortens answers.
Longest subarray with sum K.alternatives: Enumerate each start and extend a running sum in O(n²) time/O(1) space.

Largest Subarray with Sum 0.problem: Return the maximum length of a contiguous subarray summing to zero (pass k=0); empty/no match returns zero.
Largest Subarray with Sum 0.approach: If prefix[i]-prefix[j]=k, subarray (j,i] sums to k. Keep the EARLIEST index of each prefix sum to maximize length. Seed prefix 0 at index -1.
Largest Subarray with Sum 0.trace: Prefixes of [1,-1,2,-2,3] are 1,0,2,0,3; zero prefix at i=3 spans four values from index 0.
Largest Subarray with Sum 0.pitfalls: Negative values invalidate ordinary sum-based sliding windows. Store prefix sums as long; overwriting earliest indices shortens answers.
Largest Subarray with Sum 0.alternatives: Enumerate each start and extend a running sum in O(n²) time/O(1) space.

Count subarrays with given sum.problem: Count all contiguous subarrays whose sum is k; return long.
Count subarrays with given sum.approach: A previous prefix must equal currentPrefix minus k. Add its frequency before inserting current prefix so empty subarrays are excluded. Seed zero with frequency one.
Count subarrays with given sum.complexity: Expected O(n) time and O(n) space.
Count subarrays with given sum.trace: Repeated compatible prefix values count multiple start positions; they must be stored as counts rather than just presence.
Count subarrays with given sum.pitfalls: The answer can be n*(n+1)/2, exceeding int. Sum prefixes also need long.
Count subarrays with given sum.alternatives: Two nested loops maintaining a running aggregate give O(n²) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Count subarrays with given xor K.problem: Count all contiguous subarrays whose XOR is k; return long.
Count subarrays with given xor K.approach: A previous prefix must equal currentPrefix XOR k. Add its frequency before inserting current prefix so empty subarrays are excluded. Seed zero with frequency one.
Count subarrays with given xor K.complexity: Expected O(n) time and O(n) space.
Count subarrays with given xor K.trace: Repeated compatible prefix values count multiple start positions; they must be stored as counts rather than just presence.
Count subarrays with given xor K.pitfalls: The answer can be n*(n+1)/2, exceeding int. Sum prefixes also need long.
Count subarrays with given xor K.alternatives: Two nested loops maintaining a running aggregate give O(n²) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
